title: Notches Visible in Print Layout but Missing After PDF Export (CLO)
content:
Previously, when I exported my graded patterns as a PDF and opened them in Adobe Illustrator, I could only see the base pattern. Now, with the updated version of CLO, when I export the PDF using **Snapshot** from the **Print Layout** section and open it in Adobe Illustrator, I can see the graded version. However, the notches from the base pattern are not transferred to the graded sizes, even though they appear in the Print Layout view. Does anyone know how to solve this?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi, I am having the same issue - no notches no matter what format I export in - can anyone help ASAP?
Reply 1: Hi, sorry, this message slipped us. Please check the replies below for the latest status. It is a bug that will be fixed. If this is a critical feature for your workflow, please downgrade to 2025.2.330 for now.

Comment 2: Hi, there's been a few reports of this type of issue since the last patch release and I don't know more yet, but if you know for sure it worked before updating, please downgrade back to 2025.2.330 for now: https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/91194e8d345c486e9837403b913341e3
Reply 1: Update: The bug has been found and is being worked on for future patches 🙂

content:
DXF And PDF Files Imported To Clo3D Do Not Work

I exported those file from Affinity Designer (Vector Drawing App)

then imported into Clo3D with these methods with default settings.

File - Import - Adobe

File - Import - DXF (It does not open this file at all. It is greyed out.)

Original file looks like this.

![5cbcd3b011174f7186ccbc87d9e53407](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/0e9416cd35894620944b04a55f00315d/images/5cbcd3b011174f7186ccbc87d9e53407Screenshot%202026-03-11%20at%2019.11.21.png)

and when I import them into Clo3D looks like these.

![dc3fdee1bfdb42e7a5e76e7e56787f0c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/0e9416cd35894620944b04a55f00315d/images/dc3fdee1bfdb42e7a5e76e7e56787f0cScreenshot%202026-03-11%20at%2019.15.09.png)

So It definitely does not work at all.

How can I do these?

Affinity Designer File

[https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/mnx9a4es4kknidja8cjmt/Affinity-Designer-File-For-Clo3D-Importing.af?rlkey=c7kckskc5nolvhwzz6mbhnu7r&st=jpkcesam&dl=0](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/mnx9a4es4kknidja8cjmt/Affinity-Designer-File-For-Clo3D-Importing.af?rlkey=c7kckskc5nolvhwzz6mbhnu7r&st=jpkcesam&dl=0)

Exported PDF File

[https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/xkunqtxr8tffijjksunqi/Exported-PDF-File-For-Clo3D-Importing.pdf?rlkey=nbhy8dbl57u0bpjhsi5vreqx1&st=blrq81ba&dl=0](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/xkunqtxr8tffijjksunqi/Exported-PDF-File-For-Clo3D-Importing.pdf?rlkey=nbhy8dbl57u0bpjhsi5vreqx1&st=blrq81ba&dl=0)

Exported DXF File

[https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/f5olc7l2455fxq89gquit/Exported-DXF-File-For-Clo3D-Importing?rlkey=0p10csccn04gh0yjukopyxwcg&st=50gjue8x&dl=0](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/f5olc7l2455fxq89gquit/Exported-DXF-File-For-Clo3D-Importing?rlkey=0p10csccn04gh0yjukopyxwcg&st=50gjue8x&dl=0)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Why DXF is Greyed Out:The file is missing the .dxf extension in your folder. Manually rename the file to include .dxf at the end. CLO 3D won't let you select it otherwise.Not seeing patterns (Join Points):CLO is struggling to interpret your file because your pant outlines are broken segments. In Affinity, select all lines forming the pant perimeter and use Layer > Geometry > Merge (or Join Curves) to create one continuous, closed loop.Clean the File:Delete all text and numbers (1, 5, 23, "ÖN", etc.) before exporting. CLO tries to turn every single digit into a separate pattern piece, which causes the "mess" and circles you see.If Affinity DXF still doesn't work:Affinity cannot export apparel-standard DXFs (AAMA/ASTM). If you have trouble importing Affinity's standard DXF, you are probably better off exporting as PDF (Digital - High Quality) from Affinity.
Reply 1: It works now. Thank you very much.
content_description: This page aims to troubleshoot and provide solutions for issues importing DXF and PDF files exported from Affinity Designer into Clo3D.

title: Warning for Designers Selling Digital Files on CONNECT
content:
Recently, I was contacted by someone claiming they want to purchase my digital artwork as NFTs after checking out my profile on connect.clo-set site. The buyer offers a high price ( 2 Ethereum cryptocurrency per art work) and then sends a link to an unfamiliar NFT marketplace. I was hesitant and decided to do some research online and found out there were many similar scams with the similar email format.

The scam usually works like this: the buyer asks you to create an account on the marketplace website they provide and upload your artwork. Then the platform requires you to pay a **“minting fee”** , typically between **$100–$500** , in order to list the NFT.

After the fee is paid, the buyer disappears and you never hear from them again. The marketplace is often newly created, has little or no reputation, and exists only to collect these fees.

Please be cautious if someone contacts you offering to buy your files for NFTs and directs you to an unknown marketplace. Legitimate buyers usually use established NFT platforms and do not require artists to pay upfront fees.

If something feels suspicious, take time to research the website and ask questions before proceeding. Sharing this warning may help protect other designers in the community.

title: No Sketchbooks Needed: How Wilhelm Grehl Engineers Fashion in CLO
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/9eed4735f3614787bc3f6a4dfe667bf0/images/9341ad26a0ae4d3789b2ae1b7677d806cvl_2026_march_user_spotlight_v1.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/9eed4735f3614787bc3f6a4dfe667bf0/images/7f96b980ee4e469991ec0fdd6882a587cvl_2026_march_user_spotlight_v3_1.png)_M_ _eet_[ _Wilhelm Grehl_](https://connect.clo-set.com/portfolio/274957/collection/collections) _, the 3D designer who skips the sketchbook entirely to engineer fashion directly in CLO. In this User Spotlight, he reveals his unique workflow of treating digital fabric like "engineering material" to achieve his signature technical aesthetic. Discover how he turns a blank 3D window into production-ready streetwear without drawing a single line._

* * *

![c4bbfbd6df75408dbed283b7398f45a3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/9eed4735f3614787bc3f6a4dfe667bf0/images/c4bbfbd6df75408dbed283b7398f45a32.jpg)

**Can you please introduce yourself and tell us a bit about your background and current work as a designer?**

I’m Wilhelm Grehl, a 3D fashion designer from Germany working mainly with CLO. I create 3D oversized streetwear designs for brands and I help them develop their ideas in 3D, bridging digital fashion designs with real industry workflows — making 3D not just a visual tool, but a full production system.

**How did you get started in 3D fashion, and what role does CLO currently play in your creative workflow?**

After studying fashion design I didn’t want to become a traditional fashion designer and I was also not good with drawing so I was looking for a way to make designs in a different way. I also wanted to travel the world and when I discovered CLO it was the right fit for me. In the beginning I created more experimental and artsy designs and renders but found my way into the freelance world and creating designs that are ready to be produced by brands.

CLO is everything in my creative workflow, I start with an idea in my head and jump right into CLO to create it. No sketching or mood board.

![3b632028836b4de38bc0216cd25f24e6](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/9eed4735f3614787bc3f6a4dfe667bf0/images/3b632028836b4de38bc0216cd25f24e6Final_pants_closeup%20%281%29.png)

**For beginners who face "blank canvas syndrome," do you have a favorite starting method?**

I always start with a block that comes closest to the garment I want to create and then go from there. I never start from scratch. Over the years I built a library of garments which I can use for my daily work.

**Your recent work shows a shift from heavy hardware to a more 'articulated' aesthetic where the pattern itself defines the silhouette. When you begin a project, do you prioritize the 2D pattern's structural logic or the 3D drape's visual impact to achieve this technical look?**

I always create the base first, which means the overall shape has to look good, and then I put in the actual design with all the details like cuts, piping, stitching etc.  


![33f4708ccc984dde83c29a810174996e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/9eed4735f3614787bc3f6a4dfe667bf0/images/33f4708ccc984dde83c29a810174996eAnarchy_amsterdam_windbreaker_front_new.png)![b7e5aadbaff34e22897c5c8324b733e6](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/9eed4735f3614787bc3f6a4dfe667bf0/images/b7e5aadbaff34e22897c5c8324b733e6Anarchy_amsterdam_windbreaker_inside.png)

**Technical wear often draws inspiration from non-fashion elements like architecture or industrial design. When translating these inspirations into CLO, how do you handle the 'materiality'? For instance, how do you simulate the tension and stiffness of technical fabrics to match your vision?**

For materiality, I spend a lot of time dialing in fabric properties instead of relying on defaults. I adjust stiffness, stretch, thickness, and pressure to simulate tension and structure — especially for technical or industrial-inspired pieces. I treat fabrics almost like engineering materials, not just textures.

**Is there one specific setting in the Property Editor (e.g., Shear, Bending, or Thickness) that you think is the "secret ingredient" for that stiff, technical look?**

That stiff, technical look comes from a combination — keep the stretch and shear values low and the bending values high. A proper thickness supports that.

![2a8811a28d7043a78b33087c558d19eb](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/9eed4735f3614787bc3f6a4dfe667bf0/images/2a8811a28d7043a78b33087c558d19ebScreenshot%20Hoodie_35.3_pattern.png)

**To achieve the 'refined realism' seen in your latest portfolio—such as clean bonding lines and complex layer stacks—which specific CLO tools or 'hidden' workflows (e.g., modular configurations, custom trims) have become most indispensable for your quality control?**

For refined realism, the key tools for me are layer cloning, precise seam control, custom trims, and very organized pattern setups. I also rely heavily on modular workflows — building pieces in clean systems so I can control complexity without breaking realism. Clean bonding lines and stacking only work if everything underneath is technically solid.

* * *

**You are actively selling your assets on CONNECT. Creating a product for others to use must be different from creating personal art. What is your top priority when creating assets for sale?**

When I create assets for others, usability comes first. I create a lot of base shapes so they can be used in CLO projects. The asset has to be easy to modify and immediately usable — not just look good in a render.

![2c0a142734884c6ab57ca19fbb31b75f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/9eed4735f3614787bc3f6a4dfe667bf0/images/2c0a142734884c6ab57ca19fbb31b75fimage.png)

**How does it feel to see your assets being used in other creators' works? Do you have any memorable moments related to this?**

I know that people are using my assets, even if I don’t see the final results. That is completely fine, because my goal is to provide a starting point for creators to build their own designs.

**You mentioned the "location-independent" lifestyle. What is the one reality check or challenge of this lifestyle that aspiring freelancers should know?**

For me there wasn't a big challenge, of course it's good if you have a steady income so you don't get into any trouble and you have to tell yourself that it's not a vacation, even though you might live next to a beautiful beach.

And you have to stay consistent. When you’re moving between countries, routines break easily — work hours shift, internet quality varies, energy levels change, and it’s on you to still deliver at a professional level no matter where you are.

The upside is real freedom. But the trade-off is that you have to build systems, habits, and financial buffers first.

It still was the best decision for me and a dream come true. I can travel the world and work my dream job every day.

![56577592cad04dce8df4c6eeaf58f640](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/9eed4735f3614787bc3f6a4dfe667bf0/images/56577592cad04dce8df4c6eeaf58f640IMG_20260224_115518_178.jpg)

**What are your future goals as a designer and a seller? Are there any new collections or projects you are currently working on?**

The current project I’m working on is a program to help 3D fashion designers build freelance income like me so they can work with their dream clients and be location independent. Besides that I’m always designing new pieces and working on client projects. That's my daily work.
content_description: Showcasing 3D fashion designer Wilhelm Grehl’s innovative CLO workflow and insights on creating technical, production-ready streetwear without traditional sketching.

title: Objects Removed
content:
Hello! I'm a fairly new user and have a project with many colorways and opened it up today to find that embroidery objects were removed from all colorways. I came across this article suggesting that CLO does this to keep files small. <https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/community/posts/15121667014937-Fabrics-deleted-from-project>  
  
Is this still accurate? And how should I best preserve my projects? Thanks!

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Closing loop here - I did end up just re-applying the pieces and have saved a few file instances of the finished garment. Really appreciate both of your attentions on this, Melody and Brooks!-7th Rank

Comment 2: Steps taken -1. Opened existing project (called pieces)2. Opened the Colorway editor via Production3. Opened the Object Browser and clicked "+ Add" to add my PNG object4. Added my PNG to the left chest pattern piece in the 2-D pattern window5. Saved project6. Reopened7. ScreenshotUnfortunately didn't seem to do the trick, only given I followed the steps correctly. Could there be any way to access previous file versions from 3/2?At the end of the day, I can re-do it but have ~258 colorways to go through and only some mass bulking edits can be applied for my use case. 😭
Reply 1: Just wanted to add that we do not recommend having so many colorways in 1 file as the file would become too heavy. Usually we recommend between 10-15 depending on how complex the style isIf you need this many colorways you would Save As multiple versions on the style once if is fully finished

Comment 3: Hi Brooks,You're understanding is 100% accurate that is correct! Thank you for your recommendation - I'm bouncing between a couple things at the moment but will circle back in the next hour or two tops to attempt your potential resolution and will provide extensive details.

Comment 4: Hi 7thrankstore!Just to make sure I'm understanding your situation correctly, you:- Added embroidery graphics to the object browser- Applied them to the pattern across colorways- Saved the project- Upon re-opening the project, the embroidery graphics are now gone across all colorways (Not showing on the 2d pattern, in the object browser, or colorway options)Is this all accurate?Like Melody said, CLO only removes unused assets upon saving, and anything that is on a pattern piece should be saved.Could you try adding the graphic, saving, closing and reopening the project once more to see if the problem persists, or if there was maybe an error when the project last saved?

Comment 5: Also might be worth noting that my logo object was not affected across any of the colorways.

Comment 6: I don't know why the chess piece is being censored but hopefully you can see the differences in the captures. 🙏🏻

Comment 7: Hi Melody!Thank you for your response! I believe I'm understanding correctly and did have them applied to a pattern. I had this pawn piece on the chest and yesterday it is no longer in my object browser. I had taken the snapshot on 3/2 only to find them gone on all colorways on 3/4.

Comment 8: Hi there! If you wish to keep the embroideries in the project file when they are not in use on any garment yet, you have to apply them to a pattern piece somewhere in the scene so they are not auto-removed from the saved file. This can be an archived, frozen, or deactivated piece somewhere that will not interfere with the rest of the components.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on managing and preserving embroidery objects across multiple colorways in CLO3D projects to prevent unintended deletions.

title: How To Add A Node From The Node In The Middle
content:
How To Add A Node From The Node In The Middle

I want to add a node from the node shown with the red arrow to the right.

I choose the both segments then the middle node with the Edit Tool.

It still adds the node FROM THE MOST LEFT.

Not the one I wanted.

???

![32f56d71cb494f74b1e912fbe247cd21](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/0209866a20ff4d3a8c4a2dd0150e4fc0/images/32f56d71cb494f74b1e912fbe247cd21Screenshot%202026-03-03%20at%2021.39.13.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: From the screenshot its difficult to tell if segment point with the arrow is on the vertical, horizontal, or both internal lines.If when you select the segment alone, only the right side is highlighted in yellow, this is the method:The Split Line Method- Use the Add Point/Split Line (X) tool.- Right-click the specific segment you want to measure. This opens the Split Line window.- Look at the 2D window. One half of your line will be Yellow, the other Blue.- To measure from the Yellow side, type your value into the Line 1 box.- To measure from the Blue side, type your value into the Line 2 box.- Confirm: Hit OK to place the point at that exact measurement.
Reply 1: When I select either of the segments of the horizontal line.The Whole line is selected.However on the vertical line both segments are selectable.I tried both entering the value to theA) Line 1 Box : It adds the node from the left.B) Line 2 Box : It adds the node from the right.However It does not add the node from the middle node.
Reply 2: If when you select the horizontal line the entire line is highlighting, that means the segment point you're seeing is only on the vertical line.The easiest way to fix this would be to add a segment point anywhere along the horizontal line, then use the edit pattern tool to drag that point to where the 2 lines cross.
content_description: This page explains how to correctly add a new node from a specific middle node in a segment using the Edit Tool, rather than defaulting to the leftmost node.

title: How To Shorten A Rectangles Edges From The Bottom At Once?
content:
How To Shorten A Rectangles Edges From The Bottom "At Once"?

Like;

The Edges are 120 cm. 

I want to do them 94 cm.

Right Click Change Length Function does not appear when both edges are selected for some reason!

I want to shorten this rectangle from the bottom at once. (Both left and right edges at once.)

Note that the left edge has added points.

![85a0e9a34ef94e5fb3571bfab8fd09b7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/731d7baf93854dbab882e4dc71df2d70/images/85a0e9a34ef94e5fb3571bfab8fd09b7Screenshot%202026-03-03%20at%2020.43.47.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi Inspoiration25,The Change Length function only works on one segment at a time. To shorten your rectangle precisely, use one of these two "precision click" methods (Right-Clicking while Left-Click dragging):Method 1: Proportional ScalingUse this to keep the points on the left side in proportion to each other.> Select the pattern with the Transform Pattern tool.> Click the vertical scale handle on the bottom of the bounding box and drag upward.> While holding Left-Click, Right-Click to open the Transform window.> Input 94 in the Height field.Method 2: Bottom-Up ShorteningUse this to shorten the piece without moving the existing points on the left.> Select only the bottom edge with the Edit Pattern tool.> Left-Click and drag the segment upward while holding Shift.> While still holding Left-Click and Shift, Right-Click to open the Moving Distance window.Input 26 in the Distance field (this subtracts 26 from 120 to reach 94).
Reply 1: Thank you very much.
content_description: This page explains how to simultaneously shorten both bottom edges of a rectangle, even when one edge has added points, in design software.
